# İznik

> A remote terminal with a cross-platform GPUI front end. Your SSH, a server on the host, panes that survive a dropped link. Linux, macOS, Windows.

Sessions, tabs and panes live in the server. One SSH channel per host carries every pane. Pane output is the pseudoterminal’s raw bytes, rendered by the application with libghostty-vt. The command line never draws a screen.

## Docs

- [The site, in markdown](https://iznik.dev/index.md): The same account as the homepage, without the page chrome.
- [Source](https://github.com/koraytaylan/iznik): The server, the client engine, the wire protocol, the GPUI application, the C ABI, and the harness that proves them. MIT license.

## Optional

- [What a host receives](https://iznik.dev/index.md#on-a-host): The files the bootstrap writes, and nothing else.
- [Snapshot downloads](https://iznik.dev/index.md#snapshot): Linux, macOS and Windows archives from the rolling `develop-snapshot` release.
- [Commands](https://iznik.dev/index.md#commands): How to run the application, the gates, and the server by itself.
- [Rust, and the name](https://iznik.dev/index.md#rust): Rust, end to end. `cargo xtask check` is the bar. A release is a list, starting with a six-hour soak. The name pokes Zellij: Moroccan mosaic, Ottoman ceramic.
